quick.summary: Why clicking through menus leads to broken servers, and the automated solution.
quick.takeaway: Define your infrastructure in a text file so every server is an exact copy.

parts.title: Stop clicking

beats.line: I made a server by clicking through menus. Do I repeat that twenty times?
Imagine a busy bakery. The baker never guesses the amounts for every cake.
They just follow a written recipe.
Exactly. They write the recipe down once, to bake endless identical cakes.
Do not click buttons. Write a recipe for your servers instead.
You mean I list the memory and storage in a text file?
Yes. A tool reads that file and builds the whole environment.
That saves a lot of clicking.
And it guarantees every server is an exact copy.
That sounds great. But what if I need to change the recipe later?

parts.cliff: Find out how to update your recipes safely.

beats.line: When you need a bigger server, you change the text file.
We call this practice infrastructure as code.
That sounds tedious. Can I just call it server recipes?
I love that. Server recipes.
So I edit the recipe, and the tool updates the real servers?
Yes. And because it is text, you can track every change over time.
Like seeing who added more sugar to the cake last week.
Exactly. You always know who changed what, and when.
So I just commit my server changes like normal software code.
Welcome to the automated future.

quiz.question: Why is it better to build servers with a text recipe?
options: It makes every server an exact copy
It makes the servers run twice as fast
It stops users from needing passwords
It removes the need for computer memory
quiz.explanation: A text recipe ensures your automated tool builds identical environments every time without human error.

quiz.question: Because server recipes are just text files, you can track their changes over time.
quiz.explanation: You can commit text files exactly like software code, creating a perfect history of who changed what.
